2. DIRECTOR AND RECREATION MANAGER REPORT

Director Johnson and Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

Commissioner Tam shared that he attended the Scouts campout last year which had more tents
and people; he asked how staff determine the maximum number of participants for the Camp Out
and why the Scout’s event allowed so many more people. Recreation Manager Covarrubias
responded that Den Leaders help manage the activities and the parents are a lot more involved; the
Division has limited staff that can oversee activities and ensure that the crowds are controlled.

Commissioner Tsai shared that she received feedback from someone who attended this year and
last year’s Camp Out that the event was much better. She also shared that her husband and daughter
attended the Memorial Day Service and said that it was very moving and touching. Recreation
Manager Covarrubias explained that staff always try to improve the event and take into
consideration survey responses.

Chairperson Yen asked if there’s a possibility to partner with the Scouts to gain extra help at the
Camp Out. Recreation Manager Covarrubias responded that this is a possibility and staff would be
open to the idea.

Chairperson Yen expressed interest in helping to engage residents on social media by advertising
events and posting event pictures. Commissioner Tsai shared that when the Community Services
account posts events with full descriptions it is really easy to screenshot or send directly to others
which is helpful.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

3. PREVIEW OF JULY IS PARKS AND RECREATION MONTH PLANS

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

Commissioner Tsai asked if there will be a capacity for the Open Swim on July 2 and if it will be free
for everyone. Recreation Manager Covarrubias explained that staff will allow the maximum capacity
allowed the pool and there will be extra lifeguards to make sure everyone is safe in the water.

Commissioner Tam asked if staff could get volunteers involved to help make some of the activities
more engaging and less of a suggestion of things to do. Director Johnson shared that with the
addition of the new facilities supervisor position, programmers will have additional bandwidth to
enhance programming.

Chairperson Yen asked if there are any other challenges besides staffing that the Commission should
be aware of before recommending new activities or events. Recreation Manager Covarrubias

  PAGE 8 of 23
 RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  SPECIAL MEETING
JUNE 12, 2023  PAGE 3 OF 4

explained that summer is a busy season due to the high number of programs, but also because staff
are busy preparing for fall. He added that staff are always willing to listen to recommendations and
suggestions, but need to keep in mind limitations to ensure that quality is maintained. Director
Johnson added that existing staff are at programming capacity and one goal for the Division is to
start a new Recreation Program Plan to see where the gaps in service levels are.

Vice Chairperson Solan shared that she is involved in several non-profits and could help coordinate
free programs led by volunteers from the non-profits. Commissioner Wu shared his concern with
staffing; he doesn’t want staff to be overburdened and have that impact services.

Chairperson Yen shared that he has been thinking about what Commissioners can do without much
staff responsibilities. He added that he thinks residents just need guidance from the Recreation
Commission on how to get involved and meet other people. Commissioner Tam asked if a
Commissioner could lead a program and advertise it on the Community Services social media.
Management Analyst Shigenaga recommended that Commissioners post programs on their social
media and then staff would repost it on the Community Services Department’s social media as a
story or post. She added that if the Commissioners partnered with the City to put on programs,
they would be added to the City’s calendar and advertised on social media as well.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

4. MULTICULTURAL SUMMER CONCERT ENTERTAINMENT, MUSIC, AND
  FOOD

Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

Commissioner Wu asked if staff have made any preliminary inquiries as to availability. Recreation
Manager Covarrubias responded that staff have not reached out to check availability. Commissioner
Tsai shared that events like these are a great step towards increasing diversity in our community
and creating awareness. Commissioner Wu recommended that the Commission come up with back-
up options to prevent staff from needing to come back for additional recommendations.

The Commission agreed upon West African Dance Ensemble, Philippine Folk, and Brazilian Folkloric
as back-up performances and Mariachi and Caribbean Reggae as back-up music genres.

Recreation Manager Covarrubias asked if the Commission has any recommendations on food trucks
for the event, as staff are looking for 4-5 trucks. Vice Chairperson Solan recommended the Korean
food truck that was at a previous event. Commissioner Wu recommended that the food reflect the
entertainment options. Recreation Manager Covarrubias responded that staff will secure the
entertainment first and look for food trucks based on the performers. Commissioner Tsai asked
how we secure food trucks. Recreation Manager Covarrubias responded that for smaller events,
the City does not charge a fee for the food trucks; all the vendors need to do is obtain a business
license.

BACKGROUND

The Community Services Director and Recreation Manager provide a monthly
report to the Recreation Commission. It provides relevant administrative,
operational, and financial updates, in addition to upcoming events, marketing
and communication efforts, and customer feedback.

DISCUSSION

Personnel Updates
  • Welcome Damien Doperoy to the CSD Team! Damien began working for
  the City on Monday, August 21 as the new Facilities Supervisor. He hails
  from the City of Sierra Madre and possesses 12 years of facilities
  maintenance experience in both public and private sector. He enjoys the
  customer service aspect of his position and is thrilled to be part of the
  team.
  • Part-time position recruitments currently underway include:
  o (1) Maintenance Assistant (Building Attendant): interviews for the
  newly funded third position are being conducted over the next two
  weeks

  PAGE 11 of 23
   o (5) Recreation Specialists: to support the early childhood program
  and the Customer Service Office at the Community Center.
  •  Farewell to Doreen Booth, a Child Development Specialist and
  Administrative Support staff for over 10 years. She was an outstanding
  steward of the Department, and her customer service skills were
  exceptional.

Update on CSD Schedule of Fees for Service
At the July 28 City Council meeting, staff presented the schedule for all CSD
fees, which had previously been presented to the Commission at the January
9, 2023 meeting. All fees were approved by Council with the exception of Lacy
Park Closure fee and the rental fees for the newly renovated Community
Center. The rental fees presented included a 3-tiered group rate structure
based on a market-oriented, competitive market analysis of 10 municipal and
private venues similar to the new building in a 20-mile radius. At that meeting,
Council directed staff to lower Group A rates back to historic levels. In
addition, they requested that staff bring this item back at the October 27
meeting with further analysis of estimated direct and indirect operating costs
per square foot benchmarked with historic fees charged.

Successful Relocation of Recreation Division Headquarters
The Recreation Division successfully relocated its operational headquarters
from the Stoneman Building to the new Community Center. This seamless
transition allowed CSD staff to welcome the public starting September 5 at 7
AM at this new location and provide continuity of service for fall program
registration and general customer service needs.

Grand Opening of the NEW San Marino Community Center!
City Council, City Administration, and CSD staff will be hosting the ribbon
cutting and building dedication ceremony on Thursday, September 28
beginning at 5:15 PM. San Marino residents and community members are
invited to join in the celebration of this newly renovated community-gathering
place. A short dedication program will be followed by tours and refreshments.
Mark your calendars and plan to join us! Registration is not required.

Operational Staff Briefings
  Aquatics
  The 2023 summer aquatics season operated from June 3 - July 30 at
  the San Marino High School. This season, the aquatics team consisted
  of (16) Water Safety Instructors / Lifeguards and (2) supervisors. The
  total number of participants during the 9-week program was 1,779 and
  is broken down as follows:
  Group Lessons:182
  Private Lessons: 174
  Open Swim: 766
  Lap Swim and Water Walking: 13
  Summer Camp Swimmers: 639
  Water Warrior Aqua-cise: 5

  There were no major accidents or incidents. Customer satisfaction
  surveys were conducted throughout the season and comments are
  summarized in the Commendations section below.

  PAGE 13 of 23
   Summer Camps
  Ten weeks of day camp were offered in the following programs: Jr.
  Explorers, Trailblazers, Freewheelers, and Lil’ Learners. The camps
  served youth ranging in age from 2 – 14. Campers participated in arts
  and crafts, games, field trips, swimming trips, nature walks, and more!
  A highlight for many of the campers was going on various field trips to
  places like Raging Waters, Universal Studios, and Adventure City.

  Summer Sunset Concert Series
  The Recreation Division successfully hosted its annual Summer Sunset
  Concert Series at Lacy Park. On July 21, The Remotes played a variety
  of catchy TV show theme songs and on August 4, Kelly Boyz Band
  performed high energy, country rock. Attendance at each concert is
  estimated between 800 - 1000 spectators. As always, the setting of the
  concerts and the time of day made for a perfect atmosphere for families
  and friends to dance and sing together.

  Multi-Cultural Concert
  In celebration of San Marino’s cultural diversity, the Recreation Division
  hosted its first ever Multi-Cultural Concert at Lacy Park on August 18.
  In partnership with the LA County Music Center, three cultural
  performances were scheduled for the evening. The first was Dancing
  Storytellers which celebrated the culture of India through interpretive
  dance. The second act was Sakai Flamenco Dancers which celebrated
  the culture of Spain with flamenco dance and music. Finally, Suave the
  Band performed a wide variety of Latin American music genres including
  salsa, merengue, and cumbias. The event also included community and
  City department informational booths as well as 5 vendors selling a
  variety of food. Attendance grew throughout the evening to
  approximately 1,200 spectators.

  Contract Classes
  The City has introduced new and diversified classes that best meet the
  needs of the community, resulting in increased participation. This
  summer, a variety of classes were offered including cooking, STEM, and
  performing arts with a total of 390 participants. One of the highlights
  was the popularity of Jr. TITAN Tennis at the San Marino Tennis Center.
  Over the course of five weeks, 100 participants ages 6-12 learned the
  basics of tennis through skills and drills training.

I am writing to provide some glowing feedback about one of your

BACKGROUND

Since 1965, the City of San Marino has been celebrating the 4th of July holiday
with a community parade and fireworks show at Lacy Park. Several key civic
groups, such as The Chamber of Commerce, Rotary Club, and City Club, have
played an integral role in keeping this beloved community tradition alive. Since
2006, the Recreation Division has been spearheading the event-day activities
inside the Park, including the fireworks show. Rotary Club has managed the
community parade for many years, and City Club has been hosting The
Pavilion since 2014.

DISCUSSION

5-Year Attendance Estimates
This year’s attendance number shows a full recovery to pre-pandemic levels.
The event had a dramatic increase of 900 attendees from the previous year.

Event Highlights
The 4th of July Celebration continues to grow in attendance and hit a 5-year
high this year. The increase in spectators is an indication that the community
continues to enjoy and support this annual tradition. Event planning, led by
the Recreation Division, takes a large amount of coordination between various
City departments, community partners, and vendors. The activities for the day
ran smoothly including: J.P. Blecksmith Memorial Run, Family Fun Zone,
Rotary Club Parade, City Club Pavilion, main stage entertainment, food
vendors, and the fireworks show.

Event Accomplishments – What Went Well
For the second year in a row, the Police Department relocated their Command
Post to the Public Works Maintenance Yard in order to expand their emergency
response tactical area. In addition, the move increased the visibility of the
Police Department and allowed for better ingress and egress of public safety
personnel.

This year, staff rented a mobile stage. In prior years, the stage was
constructed on site and took an entire day to complete. With the mobile stage,
the amount of set-up time and physical impact on the park turf was greatly
reduced.

Event Challenges – What Didn’t Go Well
The post-event debrief meeting with the Event Committee and Executive
Team resulted in a productive conversation addressing the various challenges
brought forward by the larger crowds. The following is a list of priority items

SUBJECT: DEVELOPMENT OF AGENDA FOR THE JOINT MEETING
  WITH CITY COUNCIL

STRATEGIC PLAN CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS

Engaged and Connected Residents
Fiscally Responsible and Transparent City Government

BACKGROUND

On Friday, September 29 from 8:30 AM - 9:30 AM, the Commission will meet
jointly with City Council to discuss relevant topics associated with current and
future service and program delivery, including potential new initiatives. The
meeting serves as a communication channel and dialogue between San Marino
elected officials and the citizen advisory body representing the community’s
interests and attitudes towards active and passive recreation and wellness
pursuits for all ages.

The benefit of this one-hour joint discussion is to provide an in-depth
examination of priority topics selected by the Recreation Commission. In
addition, this meeting brings together a collective range of ideas and expertise
to the public decision-making process. It also offers training for emerging civic
leaders.

Over the past year, staff have worked with the Commission to receive
feedback related to improvements to service delivery, addressing gaps in
service, assessing resource allocation (facilities, staffing levels, operating
budget, etc.), and ultimately working to chart a new course or roadmap for
the Recreation Division post-pandemic.

  PAGE 21 of 23
 DISCUSSION

The following list represents a synthesized summary of questions, comments,
and concerns expressed by Commissioners over the past year. The goal for
the Commission today is to define an agreed upon list, using the list below as
a starting point, to submit as a draft agenda for the joint meeting with Council
on Friday, September 29.

  1. City-owned Recreation Facilities vs. Use of SMUSD facilities
  a. The Commission understands that the City has: limited indoor /
  outdoor recreation spaces; no indoor gym, fitness center, or pool;
  and no outdoor athletic fields or courts. The Commission
  understands that programming cannot expand without access to
  additional facilities.
  b. Is there interest in the wider community to facilitate expanded
  gym, pool, and athletic field space usage to expand programming
  for all ages?

  2. Stoneman Property
  a. What role will the Commission play in advocating that this
  property remains a recreation amenities site?

  3. Updated Lacy Park Master Plan
  a. What role can the Commission play in the implementation of, or
  updates to, the existing Lacy Park Master Plan, including a funding
  plan for improvements?

  4. New Programming / Service Opportunities
  a. Are there specific programming and / or service areas the
  Commission would like to recommend for consideration next fiscal
  year (July 2024 – June 2025)?

  5. NEW 3–Year Recreation Needs Assessment and Program Plan
  a. Last one was conducted by GreenPlay, LLC in January 2020
  ($30K)
  b. Included a Community Needs Assessment Survey with Key
  Findings
  c. Provided 3-year programming roadmap for Spring 2020 – Spring
  2023
  d. FY 2023-24 Priority Initiatives are:
  i. Newly Renovated Community Center
  ii. NEW Community Building Programs

  PAGE 22 of 23
 RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission review, discuss, and select priority topics
of discussion for the Joint City Council and Recreation Commission meeting on

recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:
